blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Video world models predict future frames from past frames and actions. They serve as simulators in which agents train, plan or are evaluated, and that humans can control interactively. They generate in the latent space of a video autoencoder, whose compression sets their cost per frame and how long each action waits to take effect. Yet world models often reuse the autoencoders of text-to-video generators, built for offline generation with no agent waiting and, without their training data and code, not retrainable at another compression. We therefore ask how, where and how much a world model should compress. We build CADRE, an open family of causal diffusion representation autoencoders spanning multiple spatio-temporal compressions. Its members differ only in a small bottleneck on frozen features and share a diffusion decoder self-distilled to one or a few steps. We train the same world model on each autoencoder in two domains, manipulation and navigation, with two environments each. CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera. Our study also leads to four findings. At strong compression, a diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression. In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the autoencoder than in the world model. Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions: temporal compression costs little when the camera is still, and spatial compression when it moves. Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt motion far more than image quality. Code, models and a live demo are at https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-10-21-cadre
blocks.zh: 视频世界模型从过去的帧和动作中预测出未来的帧. 它们充当模拟器,使特工在其中训练,计划或评价,人类可以交互控制. 它们在一个视频自动编码器的潜在空间中产生,其压缩确定了每个帧的成本,以及每个动作等待生效的时间。 然而,世界模型往往重复使用文本到视频生成器的自动编码器,这是为离线生成而建造的,没有代理等待,没有其培训数据和代码,就无法在另一次压缩时重新培训。 因此,我们问世界模式应如何、在何处和多少压缩。 我们建立了CADRE,一个开放的家族,由因果传播代表自动编码器组成,跨越了多个时空压缩. 其成员只在冰冻特征上的小瓶颈上存在差异,并共享可扩散解码器自分解到一或几个步骤. 我们在每个自动编码器上,在操纵和导航两个领域训练同样的世界模型,每个领域有两个环境。 CADRE构成了大多数耐久质量的前沿,尤其是带有移动相机. 我们的研究还得出了四项结论。 在强压缩时,扩散解码器比能感回还尖. 在机器人操纵中,时间压缩在自编码器中比在世界模型中更有效. 操纵和导航需要相反的压缩:相机静时时间压缩成本很小,移动时空间压缩成本很小. 出人意料的是,用一台静相机,相近的空间符号会伤害运动,远超过图像质量. 代码、模型和现场演示见https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-10-21-cadre。

blocks.en:
A world model is a learned simulator of an environment ( Ha & Schmidhuber, 2018 ) . Given past frames and an agent’s actions, a video world model generates the next frames, and can be used to train agents ( Hafner et al., 2025 ; Alonso et al., 2024 ) , evaluate robot policies ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , plan the outcome of actions ( Bar et al., 2025 ) , or simply play a game ( Bruce et al., 2024 ; Valevski et al., 2025 ; Hu et al., 2026 ) .
To enable all these applications, two different aspects have to be optimized: the throughput that measures the number of frames generated per second, and the latency that measures the delay between the action and its effect on the output.
Throughput limits how fast a simulation can happen, whereas latency limits how reactive and faithful a simulation can be.

世界模型是环境的学习模拟器(Ha & Schmidhuber, 2018). 鉴于过去的帧和代理行为,视频世界模型生成下帧,并可用于培训代理(Hafner等,2025;Alonso等,2024),评价机器人政策(Yang等,2024),计划行动结果(Bar等,2025),或只是玩游戏(Bruce等,2024;Valevski等,2025;Hu等,2026).
为了能够实现所有这些应用,必须优化两个不同的方面:测量每秒生成的帧数的吞吐量,以及测量动作与其对输出的影响之间的延迟的耐用性.
吞吐量限制了模拟发生的速度,而耐久性则限制了模拟的反应力和忠诚度。

blocks.en:
Most video world models operate in the latent space of a video autoencoder ( Bruce et al., 2024 ; Valevski et al., 2025 ) .
To avoid designing an ad hoc autoencoder, many methods ( He et al., 2025 ; Li et al., 2025a ; Zhu et al., 2026a ) reuse the autoencoder of a text-to-video generator such as LTX-2 ( HaCohen et al., 2026 ) , Wan 2.2 ( Wan et al., 2025 ) or HunyuanVideo ( Kong et al., 2024 ) .
They thus inherit the throughput and latency that come with it.
Yet, such autoencoders were not designed with the throughput-latency trade-off of world models in mind, and often perform massive temporal compression since it has low impact on visual quality.
A typical 8 × 8{\times} temporal compression delays every action by at least 400 ms at 20 frames per second. Humans
notice when their own movement appears more than about 230 ms late ( Shimada et al., 2009 ) ,
and interaction feels immediate only below 100 ms ( Miller, 1968 ; Claypool & Claypool, 2006 ) .
This raises the question of how other throughput-latency trade-offs affect rollout quality and action following.

Interestingly, our study points to four findings. (1) At strong compression, a diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression, and a few-step flow model trained by progressive self-distillation is a good fit. (2) In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the
autoencoder than in the world model: patching inside the world model loses detail,
and at eight frames also action following. (3) Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions. In manipulation the camera is still, so
temporal compression costs little while spatial compression is costly. In navigation the camera moves and the balance
reverses, so it pays to keep frames and compress spatially, the low-latency choice. (4) Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt motion far more than image quality, and, in robot manipulation, action following too.

Studying compression means training the autoencoder at many compression points. The autoencoders of
text-to-video generators release their weights but not their training data or code, so they cannot be retrained. We instead design an open family of autoencoders for world models, one per
compression point (Figure 3 ). Its members share one recipe, differ only in their
compression and are each trained from scratch, so the world models trained on them differ by compression alone.

blocks.en: 3.1 Architecture
blocks.zh: 3.1 建筑

blocks.en:
Frozen features and one trained layer encode the clip. As in MIRA ( Hu et al., 2026 ) , the encoder is that of a representation
autoencoder ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) . A frozen DINOv3
extractor ( Siméoni et al., 2026 ) encodes each frame into one feature per p × p p{\times}p patch, aggregating several
layers as in RAEv2 ( Singh et al., 2026 ) . One trained 3D convolution with
kernel ( τ , k , k ) (\tau,k,k) and stride ( τ , s ′ , s ′ ) (\tau,s^{\prime},s^{\prime}) compresses τ \tau frames of s ′ 2 s^{\prime 2} patches into a deterministic
latent, with s = p ​ s ′ s=p\,s^{\prime} (Appendix B ).

A causal diffusion decoder keeps textures sharp. A strongly compressed latent keeps a scene’s layout and semantics but little texture, so a perceptual regression decoder
averages the textures consistent with it into a blur ( Xu et al., 2026 ) . We therefore use a diffusion
decoder ( Preechakul et al., 2022 ; Pernías et al., 2024 ; Chen et al., 2025d ) ,
which samples the clip conditioned on the latent. It is a space-time-factorized
transformer ( Bertasius et al., 2021 ; Arnab et al., 2021 ) on a q × q q{\times}q patch grid, whose blocks attend over space, then causally over time. Most blocks process one token per latent frame, that is,
per τ \tau video frames. A linear map then splits each token into τ \tau tokens, one per frame, so the last blocks
resolve motion within a latent frame. The latent conditions the diffusion decoder in three places: (i) lifted by a transposed convolution and summed with the patchified noisy clip, (ii) through
a spatial AdaLN ( Park et al., 2019 ; Zhu et al., 2020 ; Dufour et al., 2022 ; Yu et al., 2026 ) in every block, which also receives the flow time t t and the jump length d d , the size of the denoising step the decoder takes (Section 3.2 , Appendix B ), and (iii) through a zero-initialized skip into a light
convolutional head. The decoder is time-causal, so it streams chunk by chunk.

blocks.en:
An autoencoder is trained to reconstruct its input, yet in latent generation, reconstruction and generation
trade off ( Yao et al., 2025 ; Hansen-Estruch et al., 2025 ) , and a
line of work shapes the latent for the generator
instead ( Leng et al., 2025 ; Kouzelis et al., 2025 ; Zheng et al., 2026 ; Xie et al., 2026 ; Ramanana Rahary et al., 2026b ) .
We therefore score rollouts instead of reconstructions (Appendix F ). As in MIRA ( Hu et al., 2026 ) ,
we judge each autoencoder by the rollouts of a world model trained on its latents; the world model, clips
and actions are shared, so only the latent varies.

blocks.en: 4.1 Should the decoder use perceptual regression or diffusion?

A decoder can regress one video from the latent or sample one by diffusion. MIRA ( Hu et al., 2026 ) takes the first route: it replaces the adversarial losses used since VQGAN ( Esser et al., 2021 ) with perceptual losses (LPIPS and DINO) and works well on Rocket League. It is also the only autoencoder besides CADRE that runs at 20 frames per second within the 230 ms lag humans notice (Figure 1 ). To test this route beyond
games, we retrain the MIRA recipe on our mixture (Appendix C ) at 2 × 32 × 32 2{\times}32{\times}32 with
our extractor and budget (Figure 4 a). Against the CADRE decoder, it gives higher PSNR but worse FID and FVD in every environment. In one step, the CADRE decoder lowers FVD by 1.4 to 2.5 × \times with similar
action following. A second step lowers FID by up to 23%.

How many frames should one latent span? Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions. In manipulation the camera is still, so
each token sees temporally redundant content: temporal compression costs little, but spatial compression loses
the small objects being handled. In navigation the camera moves, so each token sees new content: temporal compression
shows seams, but spatial compression costs little because the whole view shifts.

blocks.en: 7 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 7 结论

blocks.en:
An interactive world model inherits its cost per frame, its action latency and much of its quality from its
autoencoder, so its compression is a design choice. To study this choice, we build
CADRE, an open family spanning seven compressions, and train the same world model on each in
manipulation and navigation. CADRE forms most of the latency-quality frontier, especially with a moving camera, and our study points to four findings. At strong compression, a
diffusion decoder is sharper than perceptual regression, even in one or two steps. In robot manipulation, temporal compression is more effective in the autoencoder
than in the world model. Manipulation and navigation call for opposite compressions: temporal compression costs
little when the camera is still, and spatial compression when it moves. Surprisingly, with a still camera, coarser spatial tokens hurt
motion far more than image quality, and, in robot manipulation, action following too.
blocks.zh:
互动的世界模式继承了每个框架的成本、行动时间和大部分质量。
自动编码器,所以它的压缩是一个设计选择. 为了研究这个选择,我们构建
CADRE,一个开放的家族,跨越了7个压缩,并且在每个单元上训练同一个世界模型
操纵和导航 CADRE构成了大多数耐久质量的前沿,尤其是用移动相机,我们的研究指出了四个结论. 在强压缩,a
扩散解码器比知觉回归更尖锐,即使在一两个步骤中也是如此. 在机器人操纵中,时间压缩在自动编码器中更有效
而不是世界模式中的那种 操纵和导航要求相反压缩:时间压缩成本
当相机静止时, 和移动时的空间压缩。 出人意料的是,用一个静相机, 更相近的空间符号受伤了
移动远不止于图像质量,在机器人操纵中,动作也随之而来.

blocks.en:
Our world models each cover one environment; whether these findings carry over to a generalist one, and to policy
training and planning, remains open. Our manipulation data use still or nearly still cameras; wrist-mounted cameras move, so our account predicts they favor the compression of navigation. We hope open autoencoders will let practitioners fit a world model’s compression
to its scenes and to the latency and throughput its users need.

blocks.en:
We study how much the autoencoder of an interactive world model compresses space and time, and whether
that compression belongs in the autoencoder or in the world model.
blocks.zh:
我们研究一个交互式世界模型的自动编码器 压缩了多少空间和时间,以及
压缩属于自动编码器或世界模型

blocks.en:
World models, from offline to streaming. A world model predicts how an environment evolves under actions. Early ones predict compact latents for
control ( Ha & Schmidhuber, 2018 ; Hafner et al., 2020 ; Micheli et al., 2023 ) ; most recent ones generate the video
itself ( Bai et al., 2024 ) , for
driving ( Gao et al., 2024 ; Russell et al., 2025 ; Carrión et al., 2025 ) ,
robotics ( Yang et al., 2024 ) , egocentric motion ( Bai et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026a ) and open scenes ( Bruce et al., 2024 ; Mao et al., 2025 ; PAN Team et al., 2025 ; Zhu et al., 2026b ) .
Most are offline, taking seconds to minutes per clip. They compare autoencoders only in that regime:
SANA-WM ( Zhu et al., 2026a ) swaps the Wan 2.1 autoencoder for LTX-2’s. An interactive world model streams instead and must render each frame before the next action
arrives. Some reach real time by rendering directly from
controls ( Kim et al., 2020 ; Menapace et al., 2021 ) or with
dedicated models ( Valevski et al., 2025 ; Alonso et al., 2024 ; Bar et al., 2025 ; Ramanana Rahary et al., 2026a ) .
Others adapt a large video generator by streaming
distillation ( Yin et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2025 ) , as
Matrix-Game 2.0 ( He et al., 2025 ) and Hunyuan-GameCraft ( Li et al., 2025a ) do. They inherit its autoencoder unchanged, at 8 × 8{\times} in space and 4 × 4{\times} in time. Their blockwise generation
also adds serial computation ( Chao et al., 2026 ) .
MineWorld ( Guo et al., 2025 ) uses discrete tokens instead. Once
generation is fast, the decoder becomes the bottleneck, which Matrix-Game
3.0 ( Wang et al., 2026b ) and WorldPlay ( Sun et al., 2026 ) prune. MIRA ( Hu et al., 2026 ) instead trains its own autoencoder and judges
it by the world model; we extend that principle along both compression axes.

blocks.en:
Diffusion and flow-based generation. Both the world model and the decoder of CADRE are diffusion models trained with flow matching. Diffusion
models ( Sohl-Dickstein et al., 2015 ; Ho et al., 2020 ; Song & Ermon, 2019 ; Song et al., 2021b ) and their refinements of sampler, schedule, loss weighting and
preconditioning ( Song et al., 2021a ; Lu et al., 2022 ; Nichol & Dhariwal, 2021 ; Kingma et al., 2021 ; Kingma & Gao, 2023 ; Hang et al., 2023 ; Karras et al., 2022 ; Karras et al., 2024b ) converge in flow matching ( Lipman et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2023 ; Albergo et al., 2025 ) ,
which regresses a velocity along an interpolant between noise and data and scales with
transformers ( Bao et al., 2023 ; Peebles & Xie, 2023 ; Ma et al., 2024 ; Esser et al., 2024 ) .
Three of its design choices interact with compression. The first is the prediction target. Noise and velocity
prediction ( Salimans & Ho, 2022 ) degrade when each token is high-dimensional,
and clean-sample prediction does not ( Li & He, 2026 ) . Our decoder outputs large pixel
patches, so it predicts the clean sample, and its wavelet loss, related to the frequency
balancing of Degeorge et al. (2026) , emphasizes the fine texture it must restore. The world model’s tokens keep
64 channels at every compression, so it keeps velocity prediction. The second is the noise schedule, whose optimum
shifts with the number of tokens ( Chen, 2023 ; Hoogeboom et al., 2025 ) ;
RAE ( Zheng et al., 2026 ) generalizes the shift of Esser et al. (2024) to the number of tokens times their channels. Our compressions
change the number of tokens by more than an order of magnitude, so our tuning shifts the schedule with each autoencoder’s latent size and token count. The third is the representation. Aligning a generator’s features to a self-supervised encoder
speeds up its training ( Yu et al., 2025 ) , as masking
does ( Gao et al., 2023 ) ; we place that prior in the autoencoder instead, and the world model
generates in the features of a frozen DINOv3.

blocks.en:
Conditioning. The world model is conditioned on actions, and how faithfully it follows them is one of our three axes. Image
generators usually strengthen adherence to their condition with
guidance ( Dhariwal & Nichol, 2021 ; Ho & Salimans, 2022 ; Kynkäänniemi et al., 2024 ; Karras et al., 2024a ) ;
we use none, so action following reflects the latent and the model alone. A condition can also be weak, as with noisy
web captions ( Dai et al., 2023 ; Podell et al., 2024 ) , and some action dimensions barely change
the image, such as the finger joints in human manipulation, which our probe cannot read even on real video. We
therefore measure action following directly, by how well an inverse dynamics probe recovers the actions from the
generated frames (Appendix E ).

blocks.en:
Evaluation. We judge each autoencoder by the world model it yields, with FID ( Heusel et al., 2017 ) and
FVD ( Unterthiner et al., 2019 ) . These metrics are fragile. FID mixes fidelity and
diversity ( Kynkäänniemi et al., 2019 ) , depends on resizing and ImageNet
features ( Parmar et al., 2022 ; Kynkäänniemi et al., 2023 ) , can disagree with human
judgment ( Stein et al., 2023 ; Jayasumana et al., 2024 ) , and moves more when the
model is retrained with another seed than when it is resampled ( Dufour et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
Video and causal generation. Video diffusion moved from pixel space ( Ho et al., 2022 ) to latents, first by inflating image
networks ( Blattmann et al., 2023 ) and then with spatio-temporal
transformers ( Yang et al., 2025b ; Kong et al., 2024 ; Polyak et al., 2024 ; Wan et al., 2025 ) ,
which denoise a whole clip at one noise level. Causal generation breaks that symmetry. Rolling
diffusion ( Ruhe et al., 2024 ) gives later frames more noise, and diffusion
forcing ( Chen et al., 2024a ) draws one noise level per frame, so the next frame is
denoised from a clean or partly noisy past. History guidance ( Song et al., 2025 ) builds
on it, and MAGI-1 ( Sand.ai et al., 2025 ) scales chunk-wise autoregression to 24B parameters.
Noise on the context ( Valevski et al., 2025 ) and training on the model’s own
rollouts ( Huang et al., 2025 ) curb drift over long horizons, and
FramePack ( Zhang et al., 2025a ) compresses the history to bound its cost. Discrete alternatives
predict quantized tokens
autoregressively ( Yu et al., 2024 ; Bruce et al., 2024 ; Wu et al., 2024 ) or
by masked prediction ( Chang et al., 2022 ) , and MAR ( Li et al., 2024 ) keeps autoregression but replaces the quantizer with a per-token diffusion loss. Our world model combines flow
matching, diffusion forcing and context noise, and stays fixed while the autoencoder varies.

The autoencoder as an object of study. In latent diffusion ( Rombach et al., 2022 ; Esser et al., 2021 ) ,
generation quality depends on the structure of the latent. A line of work improves it at a fixed generator
(Section 4 ).
Representation autoencoders go further and generate in the space of a frozen self-supervised
encoder ( Zheng et al., 2026 ; Singh et al., 2026 ) ,
for text-to-image ( Tong et al., 2026 ) , low-dimensional
latents ( Gao et al., 2026b ; Shi et al., 2026 ; Bi et al., 2026 ) and video ( Xie et al., 2026 ; Guo et al., 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026 ) ,
on encoders such as
DINO ( Caron et al., 2021 ; Oquab et al., 2024 ; Siméoni et al., 2026 ) and V-JEPA 2 ( Assran et al., 2025 ; Mur-Labadia et al., 2026 ) . Distilling
such an encoder into the latent, as in GAIA ( Hu et al., 2023 ; Russell et al., 2025 ) and Mimi ( Défossez et al., 2024 ) , follows the same idea and makes
latents easier to diffuse. These works use one compression rate; our representation autoencoders vary it in space and time,
one trained autoencoder per compression point.

Video autoencoders and strong compression. Video autoencoders use causal 3D convolutions ( Yu et al., 2024 ) . Most settle
at 8 × 8{\times} in space and 4 × 4{\times} in
time ( Yang et al., 2025b ; Wan et al., 2025 ; Kong et al., 2024 ) .
Others compress harder: LTX-Video ( HaCohen et al., 2024 ) ,
DC-AE ( Chen et al., 2025b ) ,
DC-VideoGen ( Chen et al., 2025c ) , H3AE ( Wu et al., 2025c ) ,
ProMAG ( Mahapatra et al., 2025 ) and
DeltaTok ( Kerssies et al., 2026 ) , down to one token per frame. Comparisons across
rates use reconstruction ( Tang et al., 2024 ; NVIDIA et al., 2025 ) or text-to-video generation ( Hansen-Estruch et al., 2025 ) . The two rates
usually move together. We vary them independently and judge each by an action-conditioned world model.

blocks.en:
Diffusion decoders and single-step generation. Pixel and perceptual losses alone blur, so autoencoders add an adversarial
loss ( Esser et al., 2021 ) , at the price of a sensitive discriminator.
Diffusion decoders are the alternative ( Preechakul et al., 2022 ; Pandey et al., 2022 ; Pernías et al., 2024 ) ,
and scale as tokenizers with a single flow-matching loss ( Chen et al., 2025d ) ,
but decode in many steps. Single-step diffusion decoders so far need a second stage or an adversarial
term ( Vallaeys et al., 2026 ; Sargent et al., 2025 ; Zhao et al., 2025 ) ;
video diffusion decoders keep the adversarial loss ( HaCohen et al., 2024 ) or several
steps ( Yang et al., 2025a ; Teng et al., 2026 ) .
Few-step generation itself comes from distillation ( Salimans & Ho, 2022 ; Luo et al., 2023 ; Sauer et al., 2024 ) and consistency models ( Song et al., 2023 ; Lu & Song, 2025 ) ;
shortcut models ( Frans et al., 2025 ) , flow maps ( Boffi et al., 2025 ) and MeanFlow ( Geng et al., 2025 ) learn it in one stage from their own predictions.
We bring that one-stage self-distillation to a causal decoder with no discriminator.

Where compression lives. A generator can also compress through its patch size.
DiT ( Peebles & Xie, 2023 ) improves as the patch shrinks, pixel-space
transformers ( Li & He, 2026 ; Hoogeboom et al., 2025 ) replace the
autoencoder with a large patch, W.A.L.T. ( Gupta et al., 2024 ) and
Latte ( Ma et al., 2025 ) find temporal patching costliest, and
FlexiDiT ( Anagnostidis et al., 2025 ) varies the patch per step. For images,
DC-AE ( Chen et al., 2025b ) finds that compressing in the autoencoder beats
patching at matched tokens. We make that comparison for a video world model.
